title: Food Chains & Habitats
description: Grade 3 Science: habitats, producers and consumers, food chains, predators and prey, and the balance of nature — with interactive food-chain games and a habitat hunt.

topics.title: Habitats: Homes in Nature
topics.concept:
A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal — the place where it finds food, water, air and shelter. Different habitats suit different living things:

  • 🌳 Forest — home to monkeys, deer, tigers and tall trees.
  • 🏜️ Desert — home to camels, cacti and snakes.
  • 🐟 Pond / water — home to fish, frogs and water plants.
  • 🌾 Grassland — home to grass, rabbits, deer and lions.

Each living thing has a body suited to its habitat — a camel for the dry desert, a fish for the water.

recap: A habitat is the natural home of a living thing.
Forests, deserts, ponds and grasslands are habitats.
Each living thing suits its own habitat.

wonder.text: A fish would not last a day in a desert. Why does every living thing have its own special place to live?

qa.a: A good habitat gives an animal everything it needs: the right food, water, air, the right weather and a safe place to shelter and raise its young.

qa.q: Can two different animals share a habitat?
qa.a: Yes! Many animals share one habitat. A pond is home to fish, frogs, insects and birds all at once — they all find what they need there.

topics.title: Producers and Consumers
topics.concept:
In every habitat, living things get food in two ways:

  • 🌱 Producers — green plants. They MAKE their own food from sunlight, water and air. They are the start of all food.
  • 🦌 Consumers — animals (and people). They cannot make food, so they EAT plants or other animals.

Because plants make food for everyone, they are the most important link in nature.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="150" fill="#f4fff8"/><text x="75" y="80" font-size="44" text-anchor="middle">🌱</text><text x="75" y="116" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#16a06a" text-anchor="middle">Producer</text><defs><marker id="pc3" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#16a06a"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#16a06a" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#pc3)"><line x1="120" y1="72" x2="190" y2="72"/></g><text x="155" y="60" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="10" font-weight="700" fill="#16a06a" text-anchor="middle">eaten by</text><text x="225" y="80" font-size="40" text-anchor="middle">🦌</text><text x="225" y="116" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#c96a10" text-anchor="middle">Consumer</text></svg>
recap: Producers (green plants) make their own food.
Consumers (animals and people) eat plants or other animals.
Plants are the start of all food in nature.

wonder.text: Plants never go shopping for food — they make their own. So where do animals get theirs?

qa.a: Because they PRODUCE (make) their own food using sunlight, in a process called photosynthesis. No other living thing on land can do this!
Humans are consumers. We cannot make our own food like plants do, so we eat plants (like rice and fruit) and animal foods (like milk and eggs).

topics.title: What Is a Food Chain?
topics.concept:
A food chain shows how energy passes from one living thing to the next as food. It always begins with a plant.

Here is a food chain in a grassland:

  • 🌱 Grass (producer) is eaten by →
  • 🦗 a grasshopper, which is eaten by →
  • 🐸 a frog, which is eaten by →
  • 🐍 a snake, which is eaten by →
  • 🦅 an eagle.

Each arrow means 'is eaten by'. The energy from the Sun moves all the way up the chain!

recap: A food chain shows how food energy passes along.
It always starts with a plant (producer).

wonder.text: The Sun feeds the grass, the grass feeds a grasshopper… where does this chain of eating end?

qa.q: Why does a food chain always start with a plant?
qa.a: Because only plants can make food from sunlight. All animals depend on that food — so the plant is always the first link in the chain.

qa.q: What does the arrow in a food chain mean?
qa.a: The arrow means 'is eaten by' and shows which way the energy flows. Grass → grasshopper means the grasshopper eats the grass.

topics.title: Predators and Prey
topics.concept:
Among consumers, some animals hunt others for food:

  • 🦁 A predator is an animal that hunts and eats other animals (lion, eagle, frog).
  • 🦌 The prey is the animal that gets hunted and eaten (deer, rabbit, insect).

Predators often have sharp teeth, claws or great speed. Prey animals may have keen senses or run fast to escape.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="150" fill="#fff6f0"/><text x="80" y="80" font-size="44" text-anchor="middle">🦁</text><text x="80" y="116" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="middle">Predator</text><defs><marker id="pp3" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#c0392b"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#pp3)"><line x1="125" y1="72" x2="195" y2="72"/></g><text x="160" y="60" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="10" font-weight="700" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="middle">hunts</text><text x="225" y="80" font-size="40" text-anchor="middle">🦌</text><text x="225" y="116" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#16a06a" text-anchor="middle">Prey</text></svg>
recap: A predator hunts and eats other animals.
Prey is the animal that gets hunted.
An animal can be a predator AND prey (like a frog).

wonder.text: A lion hunts a deer to eat. What do we call the hunter, and what do we call the hunted?

qa.q: Can an animal be both predator and prey?
qa.a: Yes! A frog is a predator when it eats insects, but it is prey when a snake eats it. Many animals are in the middle of the food chain.
Predators keep the number of prey animals from growing too large. Without them, there could be too many deer or rabbits, and not enough plants for all.

topics.title: Keeping Nature in Balance
topics.concept:
Every living thing in a habitat is connected. They depend on one another, so nature stays in balance.

  • If frogs vanish, insects (their prey) increase too much.
  • And snakes (which eat frogs) have less food.
  • One small change affects the whole chain!

That is why we must protect nature — keep habitats clean, do not harm animals, and plant trees. Every living thing has its place.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="160" fill="#f4fff8"/><text x="150" y="50" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🌱</text><text x="80" y="120" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🐰</text><text x="220" y="120" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🦅</text><g stroke="#9ccb9c" stroke-width="2"><line x1="150" y1="60" x2="90" y2="108"/><line x1="150" y1="60" x2="210" y2="108"/><line x1="100" y1="120" x2="200" y2="120"/></g><text x="150" y="150" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#16a06a" text-anchor="middle">All living things are connected</text></svg>
recap: Living things in a habitat depend on each other.
One change can affect the whole food chain.
We protect nature by keeping habitats clean and safe.

wonder.text: If all the frogs in a pond disappeared, what do you think would happen to the insects and the snakes?

qa.q: Why should we not harm even small creatures?
qa.a: Even tiny creatures like bees and worms are important links. Bees help plants make fruit, and worms make soil healthy. Harming them upsets nature's balance.

qa.q: How can children help protect habitats?
qa.a: Keep parks and ponds clean, never throw plastic in water, do not disturb nests or animals, and plant trees. Small kind acts protect many homes in nature.

options: The natural home of a living thing
questions.explanation: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal naturally lives.
Plants produce (make) their own food, so they are producers.

questions.q: In a food chain, the arrow means…
questions.explanation: The arrow shows 'is eaten by' — the direction energy flows.

questions.q: An animal that hunts others is a…
questions.explanation: A predator hunts and eats other animals.

questions.q: Which animal lives in a desert habitat?
questions.explanation: A camel is built for the dry, hot desert.

questions.q: A food chain always begins with a…
questions.explanation: Plants make food from sunlight, so they start every food chain.

questions.q: Why can a frog be BOTH a predator and prey?
options: It eats insects but is eaten by snakes
questions.explanation: A frog hunts insects (predator) but is hunted by snakes (prey).

questions.q: If all the frogs in a pond disappeared, what would happen?
options: Insects would increase and snakes would have less food
questions.explanation: Frogs' prey (insects) would grow too many, and snakes (which eat frogs) would have less food.

questions.q: Why are producers the most important link?
options: They make the food that all consumers depend on
questions.explanation: Plants make the food that every consumer in the chain depends on.

questions.q: Order this food chain correctly: frog, grass, snake, grasshopper.
questions.explanation: Energy flows: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake.

questions.q: Why should we protect even bees and earthworms?
options: Bees help plants fruit and worms keep soil healthy — both keep nature in balance
questions.explanation: Bees and worms are important links that keep nature healthy and in balance.
